summary:
# Project Summary

A multiplayer, first-person space simulation game where up to four players work together to complete a space mission. Players must prepare their spacecraft, manage limited resources, operate essential onboard systems, navigate through space, overcome unexpected emergencies, and collect scientific research at their destination.

Each player receives randomly generated character traits, cognitive characteristics, and physical or psychological limitations that influence their gameplay. These differences encourage teamwork, communication, and the distribution of responsibilities according to individual strengths.

Players must actively control spacecraft systems, including life support, navigation, propulsion, electrical power, and environmental monitoring. An interactive mission handbook provides real physics formulas, technical references, operational limits, and a calculator that players use to solve scientific problems throughout the mission.

The game also features a budget and resource management system, random technical malfunctions, and external space hazards. Its main educational goal is to help players understand the complexity of real space missions through hands-on problem-solving, scientific calculations, engineering challenges, and cooperation.
details:
Our project is a web-based multiplayer, first-person space simulation and survival game designed for up to four players. The main objective is to successfully complete a space exploration mission through teamwork, scientific problem-solving, and spacecraft management. Players join a private multiplayer room using a unique access code, with each participant controlling one astronaut.

The gameplay is divided into three main stages: mission preparation, spaceflight, and arrival at the destination. During preparation, players receive a limited budget and must decide how to purchase essential equipment, distribute resources, and prepare the spacecraft for launch. During the flight, they must actively operate different spacecraft systems, monitor technical parameters, perform scientific calculations, navigate through space, and respond to unexpected emergencies. Upon reaching their destination, players must complete research objectives and collect scientific data.

A distinctive feature of the game is its random character card system. At the beginning of each mission, players receive randomly assigned cognitive, psychological, personality, and physical characteristics that influence how they perform certain tasks. These characteristics can introduce both advantages and limitations, encouraging players to recognize individual strengths, distribute responsibilities, and support one another.

Players are responsible for operating essential spacecraft systems, including radar and proximity sensors, life-support systems, oxygen supply, CO₂ filtration, temperature and humidity regulation, navigation displays, attitude and movement controls, measurement instruments, and engines. Each system has specific operational parameters that players must monitor and maintain within established limits.

An interactive mission handbook provides players with technical instructions, normal operating ranges, real physics formulas, and a built-in calculator. Instead of relying entirely on automated solutions, players must independently apply scientific knowledge to solve problems involving orbital velocity, gravity, acceleration, energy consumption, and navigation.

The game also incorporates resource and budget management mechanics. Players must carefully distribute limited electrical power, fuel, oxygen, and other supplies. They can purchase additional equipment, such as backup batteries, medical kits, cooling supplies, and CO₂ filtration cartridges. Their decisions directly affect the spacecraft's ability to withstand emergencies.

Throughout the mission, players encounter unpredictable events, including equipment malfunctions, electrical failures, communication disruptions, orbital debris, and space radiation hazards. These challenges require quick decision-making, effective communication, and cooperation.

The main educational purpose of the project is to help players understand how real space missions operate, what challenges astronauts face, and why physics, mathematics, engineering, and teamwork are essential for successful space exploration. By combining interactive spacecraft operations with scientific problem-solving and multiplayer cooperation, the game transforms space education into an immersive and practical learning experience.
